WB01.why: Cited. Reduces degree via the quadratic (x + 1/x); WB01 raises degree and reduces x^3 twice. Different ask.
Not cited. Evaluate an expression from a given quadratic-type relation without solving. Same family; different algebra.

WB02.why: Not cited. [f(1 + h) - f(1)]/h for f(x) = x^2: same symbolic-shift-and-subtract mechanism, but numeric base point and divided by h. Allowed; keep apart.

WB03.why: Cited. Zeros + y-intercept -> a + b + c. WB03 reverses (coefficient sums -> zeros) and asks the minimum. Close; keep apart.

WB04.why: Cited. Reflection across a vertical line of an exponential; WB04 is a horizontal line y = 5 on a quadratic. Allowed.
Not cited. Same f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7 in SAT-000155 (g(x) = f(x + 3), minimum asked). Same function, different transformation; consider changing f to avoid the reused polynomial.
Not cited. Point reflected across a line y = x + 1. Different object.

WB05.why: Not cited. Sum/difference of two rational expressions that both factor and partially cancel; 0 is a distractor there. Same family; keep apart.

WB06.why: Not cited. 'f(x) = a*b^x, a, b positive. If f(2)*f(4) = 144, what is f(3)?' (12). WB06 is f(1)*f(3) = 144 -> f(2) = 12: identical mechanism, identical ask, same 144 and 12. Drop.
Not cited. f(2)*f(4) = 144 and f(5) = 48, find f(1): the bank already uses the geometric-mean step as step 1 of a longer item. WB06 is that step alone.

WB07.why: Cited. Agree: adding the constant changes the key step.
Not cited. f(x) = x^3 - 4x evaluated at -2 and 3 (same odd cubic). Different ask; keep apart.

WB08.why: Not cited. f(x - 1) = x^2 + 2x, find f: substitution of a linear expression into the same x^2 + 2x. Inverse direction; keep apart.

WB09.why: Not cited. f(x) = 3*2^x and g(x) = f(x + k): same 'a shift multiplies by the base' insight with the same function 3*2^x. Different ask; keep apart.

WB10.why: Cited. Agree; four-factor pairing is new.

WB11.why: Not cited. 2^(x+1)*3^(x-1) = 16: combining unlike bases into one power (6^x). WB11 combines 8 and 25 into 200^(x-2). Same 'merge unlike bases' move; different finish.
Unlike-base exponential equations (numeric) and common-base matching. Allowed.

WB12.why: Not cited. Symmetry of a quadratic about its axis. Different ask.
Cited. 'Must be true' with sign conditions. Keep apart from 000905 (batch-081).

WB14.why: Not cited. '(3x - 2)^2 - (x + 1)(9x - 5)' -> -16x + 9 with distractor -4x + 9 (undoubled middle term): expand a binomial square, subtract a quadratic with the same leading term so x^2 cancels, ask the linear equivalent. WB14 is the same item made easier. Drop.
Not cited. '(2x - 3)^2 - (x + 1)^2' - same (2x - 3)^2 expansion and same ask with an extra square.

WB15.why: Not cited. Interval where a quadratic is negative. WB15 adds 'falling'. Keep apart.
Not cited. Zeros -1 and 5, interval answer from a quadratic. Keep apart.

WB16.why: Not cited. 'P(t) = 1,000*2^(t/5). How many years after 2020 is the population 700% greater?' Same mechanism (convert 'X% greater' to the factor 1 + X/100, then solve the exponential), same ask (time), same trap (reading 'increased by' as the factor). Drop.

WD01.why: Not cited. 'Two circles have the same center, radii 9 and 12. Two radii of the larger circle form a 60 deg central angle. The region between the two circles inside this angle has area k*pi. Find k.' WD01 copies the setup and wording and reverses the ask (area given, radian angle asked). Close only because the ask is inverted; very near. Cite it and keep in a different batch.
Cited (000186 not cited: whole ring area). Agree.

WD02.why: Not cited. AB a diameter, angle 30 deg, area 18*sqrt3 -> radius 6. WD02 is the reverse 30-60-90-in-a-circle computation (radius -> area) with an arc-ratio front end. Keep apart.

WD03.why: Not cited. 'The line y = x + 7 intersects the circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 at two points. What is the distance between those two points?' Same line, same circle family, same ask (chord length); only r changes (25 -> 169). Cross-exam re-skin. Drop.

WD04.why: Point with equal distances, sum of x-coordinates; different condition. Allowed.

WD05.why: Not cited. Right triangle with hypotenuse AB = 10, trig condition, area asked, answer 24. Different trig condition (sin A = cos B) but identical numbers and answer. Change numbers.
Not cited. sin(2 theta) = 2 sin theta cos theta: the sin*cos product. Different context.

WD06.why: Not cited. 'Point P lies inside rectangle ABCD... distances from P to A, B and C are 3, 4 and 5. What is the distance from P to D?' (3*sqrt2). Identical numbers, mechanism and ask. Cross-exam duplicate. Drop.

WD07.why: Not cited. Circle through (1, 2), (13, 2), (1, 7): legs 12 and 5, radius 6.5 = half the hypotenuse. WD07 asks CM, which is that same circumradius, with the same 5-12-13 triangle and the same answer 6.5. Different ask on paper; same fact and number. Change the triangle and keep in a different batch.

WD08.why: Cited. No coordinate-square-vertex item found in either bank.

WD09.why: Not cited. s = r*theta with numbers (2.5 rad, find r) and a 2-radian sector. WD09 is the no-numbers definition version. Allowed.

WD10.why: Not cited. Point D on a leg of a right triangle with a condition, length asked. Different condition.

WD11.why: ACT-319 cited (same r = 3, h = 10, lateral area). ACT-736 not cited (total surface area, r = 3). Half-cylinder new face is new. Consider different dimensions from ACT-319.

WD13.why: Cited (ACT-309 pyramid volume not cited). Corner-pyramid removal is new.

within_list_cues.WB01: Calculator route: solve x^2 = 2x + 1 numerically and evaluate -> 2.0000. SPR, so not a giveaway, but 'hard' is generous; trap 7 has no derivation (7 - 5x is not 7) - replace it.
within_list_cues.WB04: x = 0 leaves A, C, D (stated). Graphing all four in Desmos is quick; acceptable for MC.
within_list_cues.WB05: Identity item: x = 0 eliminates every distractor (B 6, C 6, D -6). Legitimate for an equivalence item, but the key '0' is guessable when the stem sums two fractions with opposite factors; B and C both equal 6 at x = 0, so test values do the whole item. Fine at easy-medium.
within_list_cues.WB06: (Dropped) b = 1 shortcut: a^2 = 144 -> f(2) = 12 with no insight (same problem noted for EB08 in ideas-058).
within_list_cues.WB07: Numeric Desmos shortcut: solve x^3 - 4x = 7 (a = 2.5891) and evaluate p(-a) = -5.000. Rate medium, not medium-hard.
within_list_cues.WB08: Identity item; t = 2 eliminates all distractors (legitimate).
within_list_cues.WB09: Direct computation of f(0..3) = 3, 6, 12, 24 gives 9 vs 4.5 in seconds; the 'shift scales by the base' insight is not needed. Rate medium.
within_list_cues.WB10: Calculator: x = -2 + sqrt10 gives the product 54.000 directly. Rate medium-hard.
within_list_cues.WB11: Key guessable without the math: x = 2 is the first value anyone tries (both exponents become 0, both sides 1); Desmos intersection gives 2 as well. Not 'hard'. Trap -2 derivation is wrong (x - 2 = -(x - 2) gives x = 2, not -2).
within_list_cues.WB12: Must-be-true check: A false (9a + k = 1 forces a = 0), B false (f(4) = f(0) = 1), C false (f(5) = f(-1)); only D is necessarily true. OK.
within_list_cues.WB13: OK. Plugging k = 6 back is a check, not a shortcut.
within_list_cues.WB15: Desmos graph shows it instantly; acceptable at medium. Key is not longest.
within_list_cues.WD01: Distractor D 5*pi/2 exceeds 2*pi, an impossible central angle; eliminable by common sense. Replace with 5*pi/8 (uses only the smaller sector, (theta/2)(16) = 5*pi; checked).
within_list_cues.WD05: Key guessable: AB = 10 with sin*cos = 0.48 invites 6-8-10 (0.6*0.8) by recognition; also identical numbers/answer to SAT-000801. Use AB = 12, sin A*cos A = 0.4 -> area = (1/2)(144)(0.4) = 28.8 (checked; sin 2A = 0.8 valid, legs not a nice triple, terminating SPR).
within_list_cues.WD07: OK on cues; numbers duplicate SAT-000953 (5-12-13, 6.5).
within_list_cues.WD08: OK: both C and D also form right angles and A is the only one equidistant from both given points and on the perpendicular bisector; one check is not enough, as intended.
within_list_cues.WD09: Easy; key 2 among 1, pi/2, 2, pi - fine.
within_list_cues.WD11: Key D 39*pi + 60 is the 'everything included' choice and the largest; a student can pick the biggest sum of all parts. Add a larger distractor, e.g. 48*pi + 60 (counts the two ends as full disks: 30*pi + 18*pi + 60), in place of A 39*pi.
within_list_cues.WD12: Distractor D 4/3 > 1 is not a possible sine value; eliminable by common sense. Replace with 4*sqrt17/17 (CD/DE, using triangle CDE with DE = sqrt68; checked) or another value in (0, 1).
within_list_cues.within_list: Three items use the 6-8-10 triangle (WD05 legs 6, 8; WD10 BC = 6, AC = 8, AB = 10; WD12 AB = 8, BE = 6, AE = 10) and WD07/WD03 use 5-12-13: vary the triangles and split across batches. WD02 and WD07 both rest on 'hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumcircle' - separate batches. WD01 and WD09 are both radian/sector items - separate. WB01 and WB10 are both 'use the given quadratic relation, don't solve' SPR items - separate. WB05, WB08 (and dropped WB14) are equivalent-expression MC items - separate. WB04 and WB15 both use vertex position read off a quadratic - separate.

math_errors.WB11: Trap -2 rationale is wrong: solving x - 2 = -(x - 2) gives x = 2. Replace or drop the trap.
math_errors.WB01: Trap 7 is not derived ('keeps only the rational part of (1 + sqrt2)^3' gives 7 - 5(1 + sqrt2), not 7). Trap 1 checks (5x + 1 - 5x = 1).
math_errors.WB06: Trap 72 ('arithmetic middle') does not follow from anything; moot since WB06 is dropped.
